2
The luminosity L of a star is given by
L = 4πr 2σT 4
where
r is the radius of the star,
T is the temperature of the star,
σ is a constant with units W m–2
K–4.
What are the SI base units of L ?
s–1
B
kg m2
s–2
C
kg m2
s–3
D
kg m2
A
kg m2
s–4

hints: Notice $r$ is a length in $\text{m}$ so $r^2$ is in $\text{m}^2$, and $T$ is temperature in $\text{K}$ so $T^4$ is in $\text{K}^4$.
Connect the units of $\sigma$, $\text{W m}^{-2}\text{K}^{-4}$, to those factors: the $\text{m}^{-2}$ and $\text{K}^{-4}$ will cancel to leave watts.
Convert the remaining watt to SI base units using $\text{W} = \text{J s}^{-1}$ and $\text{J} = \text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2}$, then combine powers of $\text{s}$.
walkthrough: Identify the units of each term in $L = 4\pi r^2 \sigma T^4$. The number $4\pi$ has no units, $r^2$ has units $\text{m}^2$, $T^4$ has units $\text{K}^4$, and $\sigma$ has units $\text{W m}^{-2}\text{K}^{-4}$.
Multiply the units: units of $L = \text{m}^2 \times \text{W m}^{-2}\text{K}^{-4} \times \text{K}^4$.
Cancel $\text{m}^2$ with $\text{m}^{-2}$ and $\text{K}^4$ with $\text{K}^{-4}$, leaving units of $L$ as $\text{W}$.
Express the watt in base units. Since power is energy per time, $\text{W} = \text{J s}^{-1}$, and $\text{J} = \text{N m} = \text{kg m s}^{-2} \times \text{m} = \text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2}$.

A.explanation: Gives $\text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-1}$, which has one power of $\text{s}^{-1}$ too few for power and does not follow from cancelling $\text{m}^2$ and $\text{K}^4$.

B.explanation: Gives $\text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2}$, which is the base unit of energy in joules, not energy per second for luminosity as power.

C.explanation: $r^2 \sigma T^4$ gives $\text{m}^2 \times \text{W m}^{-2}\text{K}^{-4} \times \text{K}^4 = \text{W}$, and $\text{W} = \text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-3}$.

D.explanation: Gives $\text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-4}$, which has one extra $\text{s}^{-1}$ factor, as if $T^4$ contributed an extra time dependence.
